summary: The note argues that plastic recycling is largely ineffective, citing an EPA report that only 8% of plastics were recycled, and blames limited capacity, material complexity, contamination, and producers' lack of accountability. It surveys alternatives including upcycling, bioplastics, production regulations with extended producer responsibility, consumer demand, and community action. It concludes that a thorough overhaul of the approach to plastics is needed.
one_line: Plastic recycling is failing due to capacity, complexity, and contamination, so alternatives like upcycling, bioplastics, producer responsibility, and community action are needed.
key_facts: On 3rd September 2023 the Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) released a report that only 8% of plastics generated in the previous year were recycled.
Local Recycling Coordinator Emily Watson says the problem is 'the lack of capacity' rather than lack of will, as facilities can't handle the volume or complexity of materials.
John Kim, plant manager of RecycleIt Inc., says sorting different plastic types is cumbersome and that a lot of what arrives is simply not recyclable.
Kim notes recyclers operate on thin margins, and manual sorting labor for complex materials makes the economics not add up.
Nonrecyclable items put in recycling bins can spoil entire batches of otherwise recyclable materials.
On 15th October 2023 recycling educator Melissa Turner said at a workshop that educational outreach must be stronger to reduce high contamination rates.
On 22nd November 2023 environmental lawyer Alex Green said at a panel on environmental accountability that producer responsibility is dire needed so companies are accountable for recyclability.
Summitville artist Sarah Grant champions upcycling, which adds value by creating something new from waste without energy-intensive breakdown.
On 5th December 2023 Sarah Grant showcased her upcycling work at a community fair.
Dr. Lisa Rodriguez, a leading researcher in biodegradable plastics, says investment in bioplastics is critical because new types that don't require recycling are needed.
Environmental advocates urge stronger production regulations that incentivize eco-friendly alternatives and impose extended producer responsibility.
Grassroots community movements educate the public, push local legislation, and start community-based recycling programs that can be replicated and scaled.
